title: Maximally entangled states are not complete for pseudo-telepathy
abstract: One of the longstanding open problems in quantum nonlocality is to determine if maximally entangled states are complete for bipartite pseudo-telepathic games: namely, if every nonlocal game which admits a perfect entangled strategy admits such a strategy which uses a maximally entangled state. We exhibit a counterexample to this in the form of a bipartite nonlocal game with input sets of size 4 and 3 and output sets both of size 6. This game is part of a new class of nonlocal games, which we call inner product games, which could be of independent interest.
summary: This paper addresses an open problem in quantum nonlocality concerning whether maximally entangled states are sufficient for all pseudo-telepathic games. The authors construct a specific counterexample game, $G_{4,3,6,6}$, and rigorously prove that this game requires entanglement beyond what is provided by any maximally entangled state. This settles the long-standing question negatively.
main_problem: The central question is whether maximally entangled quantum states are sufficient (complete) to guarantee a perfect strategy for every bipartite pseudo-telepathic nonlocal game.
main_result: The authors provide a counterexample, $G_{4,3,6,6}$, demonstrating that maximal entanglement is not always sufficient for such games, settling the open question negatively.
method: The proof involves constructing an inner product game and using advanced mathematical techniques, including the NPA hierarchy relaxation solved via SDP, to show the non-existence of a perfect maximally entangled strategy.
model_or_system: The study uses bipartite nonlocal games, specifically a newly defined class called 'inner product games,' involving input/output sets of sizes 4, 3, and 6 respectively. The analysis is based on quantum correlation measures derived from unitary operators.
key_observables: The existence or non-existence of a perfect strategy (probability one) using either an entangled state or a maximally entangled state for the game $G_{4,3,6,6}$.
important_parameters: Input set sizes (4 and 3), output set size (6), and the specific unitaries defining the inner product games.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on solving a complex SDP derived from assuming the existence of such a state, which is computationally intensive and formalized in Lean.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem context regarding completeness for pseudo-telepathy, constructs the specific counterexample game $G_{4,3,6,6}$ (an inner product game), and then proceeds through mathematical machinery (NPA hierarchy/SDP) to prove that no perfect maximally entangled strategy exists.
why_interesting: This work pushes the boundaries of understanding quantum correlations by providing a concrete counterexample in nonlocal games, which has deep implications for characterizing genuine multipartite entanglement beyond simple state characterizations.
